question: What makes partial document input stable, cancelable and reversible, and should the current AI-specific update owner be replaced by a neutral contract?
trigger: User asked to reconcile streaming after the September 28–30 conversion and preview work, defer search, and identify the next ledger item. Metadata-only; no downstream implementation or fresh AI audit requested.
requirements: Incremental previews preserve the value and diagnostics of a fresh partial parse; invalidation can require a whole parse.
Completion and deliberate stop strictly parse the accumulated source; cancellation and replacement must prevent stale scheduled publication.
Markdown owns parsing and continuation provenance. Consumers own transport, accumulated source, cancellation, publication cadence, acceptance and undo.
Non-AI streaming works through the same parser contract. Preview work does not create accepted-document history entries.

Keep historical source identities, failed measurements, and review/adoption/proof separate. Reconcile existing work without inventing a new implementation outcome or rerunning settled architecture research.
evidenceReuse: Read the current Markdown API and non-AI demo, reconciled the amendment and adoption records plus subsequent document/static/root repairs, and consumed a bounded read-only source/receipt mapping. Existing browser and benchmark observations keep their original scopes and snapshot identities. No tests or browser matrix were rerun in this reconciliation.
summary: Stop proposing another generic streaming owner. The adopted Markdown parseSlice previous-result hint supplies neutral incremental parsing, while the non-AI demo owns abort, cadence and strict finalization and AI owns acceptance/undo. September 10 AI-dependent-demo wording is superseded by current source and recorded conversion adoption. Retain converted-segment reuse and coherent immutable preview views; preserve conservative invalidation and explicit remaining proof limits. This scope gains review coverage, not a retroactively rebound implementation receipt.

alternatives: Keep existing owners: current Markdown continuation plus consumer-owned lifetime covers both the independent demo and AI preview without another protocol.
Add a neutral public stream handle/controller: it duplicates the consumer abort/source/cadence state and relocates product acceptance and undo without a demonstrated independent coordination job.
Move cancel/accept/undo into Markdown or Plite: parsing does not own request validity, product review or accepted-document history; this would couple independent jobs.

Replace the parser or promise unconditional tail-only work: definitions and extensible/stateful mappings can invalidate earlier output; current conservative fallbacks preserve the selected dialect and prefix oracle.

Delete the streaming scope as a duplicate of conversion-boundary: keep it as a semantic retrieval address for consumer lifetime, and link the existing immutable work instead of duplicating implementation history.
proofLimits: Source and recorded-evidence reconciliation only. Original conversion, Markdown and HTML execution outcomes are not rebound to streaming; its generated adoption/proof progress remains unbound. Existing Chromium contract/lifetime evidence is bounded to its recorded snapshots, not all providers, native input or browsers. The earlier pp4 AI assessment changes the attribution guard from 1.20 to 1.25; the latest content-root matrix retains six complete cells and two ai-rich cells with passing latency/text but inconclusive CPU profiles. Full retained-markup interaction is not driven, and the known narrow-view AI review/undo browser failure remains open. No package suite, browser, benchmark or product mutation in this task.
